Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem export: SIEM handoff, sample logs, and retention questions

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for yesterday's call. Medusa is ready to move from the design phase to a short operational handoff for our on-prem collectors. A few priority items for the upcoming integration that we need Redwood to confirm: 

- HEC vs syslog: we plan to ship via a Splunk HEC endpoint inside our VPC. Can Redwood accept a private HEC URL (mTLS) or do we need an outward-facing proxy?
- Token cadence: we require rotation of tokens every 24 hours and short-lived tokens are preferred. What's Redwood's support for ephemeral credential exchange (signed assertions / OIDC)?
- Trace correlation: we will attach a correlation header (X-MEDUSA-TRACE) in our application traces; need docs on Redwood's tracehook header mapping and a sample span schema.
- PII handling: we will mask PII before export, but Redwood should confirm whether any extra suppression is required for telemetry used in QA.
- Evidence: can you provide the export runbook and an example evidence diagram? We attached a small sample of logs for format checks.

Target: production-ready export (non-prod validation + 2-week pilot) starting Mar 28.

Assignees: please loop security and infra.

Best,
Alan
Security Engineering
Medusa Corp
Attachments: medusa_sample_logs.tar.gz (text/syslog sample)
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>

Cc: glen@cysecpartners.com, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem export: SIEM handoff, sample logs, and retention questions

Hi Alan — great to see the sample logs, thanks. High level answers and next steps below. I'll kick off an internal ops runbook update and loop in security/infrastructure for specifics.

Quick answers:
- HEC endpoint: Redwood can receive events via a privately provisioned HEC inside the customer's VPC using mutual TLS. We prefer the collector to POST to an internal load-balanced HEC endpoint. If customers cannot expose an HEC, we can accept syslog over TLS to an Edge Forwarder.
- Token rotation: we support short-lived tokens via brokered OIDC assertions. For your token rotation cadence (24h) we recommend using ephemeral HEC tokens issued by your token exchange service; Redwood will accept tokens with up to 1-hour clock skew.
- Trace correlation: include the X-MEDUSA-TRACE header on trace ingest and we will map it to trace.context.correlation_id. I will share a tracehook sample and a small JSON schema in the follow-up.
- PII: Redwood's pipeline will not attempt to re-identify masked fields; we'll add a validation step to assert required fields are redacted during the pilot.

Next steps:
1) Internal kickoff: I'll forward this thread to our infra and security teams for runbook items and required evidence.
2) Runbook & diagram: infra to produce export_playbook_v1.2.pdf and an evidence_handoff_diagram.png.
3) Exchange test credentials and schedule a dry-run on Mar 25 (non-prod) and pilot on Mar 28.

Can you confirm the non-prod bucket/HEC URL and a point-of-contact for your infra (IP allowlist + egress rules)?

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Principal Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Thanks for the ping — a few security guardrails and evidence items for the runbook: 

- Crypto & endpoints: require TLS1.2+ with mutual auth (client cert rotation cadence aligned with Medusa's security policy). Preferred cipher suites are listed in the attached evidence_handoff_diagram.png.
- Token exchange: support OIDC-issued short-lived tokens (we will validate iss/aud and exp). For HEC we should accept bearer tokens with an additional signed assertion from Medusa's token broker.
- Audit evidence: capture request/response metadata for all HEC interactions for a minimum of 90 days (this can be extended per contract). Evidence should include request timestamps, token id hash (not raw token), client cert fingerprint, and routing decision logs.
- Data handling: confirm that telemetry ingest retains the redacted fields as redacted (store as masked-string). No re-identification operations will be allowed without an explicit, auditable process request.

I'll attach a short checklist and the evidence diagram. We will need SOC2 mapping for the pilot; I can draft that if you provide the token exchange design.

-Kimberly
Director, Security & Compliance — Redwood Inference
Attachments: evidence_handoff_diagram.png

Folks — draft runbook notes and actions below. I'm attaching export_playbook_v1.2.pdf as the initial operational doc. Highlights and actionable items for the Mar 25 dry-run: 

1) Network & LB topology
- Provision internal NLB (HEC LB) in Medusa's VPC with sticky session disabled. Health checks on /_health returning 200 within 250ms.
- Allow inbound from Medusa collector subnet (will provide CIDR) to HEC port 8088 over mTLS (mutual TLS). No public egress required.

2) Throughput & batching
- Target: 300 EPS sustained, allow burst to 1200 EPS. Use our batching window 250ms / up to 10k tokens per batch. Configure collector to buffer up to 10s for large bursts during batch jobs.

3) Auth & token exchange
- Support OIDC brokering: Redwood exposes a token-accept endpoint that validates signed assertions. Tokens short-lived (1h) recommended during pilot; Medusa's 24h rotation acceptable if using a refresh assertion pattern.

4) Tracing & correlation
- Map X-MEDUSA-TRACE -> trace.context.correlation_id. Include a span processor that attaches redwood.trace.origin=medusa. Sampling: default p50 latency target preserved by dropping at source when EPS > 2000 to prevent backpressure.

5) Observability & retention
- Ingest metadata: token_id_hash, client_cert_fingerprint, request_id, route. Retention: default 90 days. Provide a compressed evidence bundle for audits (audit bundle generation in export_playbook_v1.2.pdf).

6) Pilot checklist (Mar 25 dry-run)
- Exchange test certs and test HEC URL
- Validate sample logs (Alan's attachment) and confirm field mappings
- Execute load test to 1.2k EPS for 3 minutes
- Validate audit bundle generation and delivery to Medusa's S3 share

Linking JIRA:OBS-4821 for runbook changes and scheduling. Please review the attached PDF before the Mar 22 sync; I'll be online at 10:00 PT.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: export_playbook_v1.2.pdf
